newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Makhteshim, Agan rated buys.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Makhteshim, Agan rated buys.

text.p: Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd and its Agan Chemicals Manufacturers ltd subsidiary, both of Israel, were rated buys by Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull (SGST).

Analyst Yuval Raviv said in report that earnings per share at Makhteshim, a maker of agro-chemicals, would grow to 1.85 shekels next year from an estimated 1.60 shekels in 1996. He put a 23 shekel price target on Makhteshim shares in 12 months' time. Makhteshim is trading at 17.75 shekels.
"Future growth at Makhteshim should be impressive with the construction of a new plant for liquid oxygen production and the development of new products in the core business," SGST said.
Raviv noted Makhesthim's high gearing, which was due to debt financing of acquisitions, but said shareholders equity "appears strong enough" and there would be little need for additional finance.

Analyst Keith Phillips gave a buy rating for Agan, a maker of crop-protection chemicals, estimating EPS would reach 5.52 shekels a share next year from an estimated 5.03 in 1996. He set a target price of 60.36 shekels in 12 months, compared with the current 50.30 shekels.
Phillips noted Agan's strength in the fast-growing Latin American market, where Agan and Makhteshim jointly acquired 49 percent of Brazil's biggest pesticide distributor.

Agan has preserved margin levels despite high growth in recent years and expects to improve on them with the introduction of new, higher-margin products. These include Lycopene, a chemical used against cancer.
Agan is now trading at 10 times 1996 earnings, which with a 2.0 percent yield, makes the shares cheap, said Phillips.
Koor Industries plans to reorganise its Makhteshim and Agan subsidiaries. The two companies will be de-listed and replaced by a holding company called MAGM Chemistry Holdings Ltd.
